memory_update.text: MIDD should be retained as the reference public-market anchor for commercial restaurant equipment, but not treated as the main underfollowed discovery target.

FARM is a below-USD-300M speculative exception with unusually direct relevance to beverage equipment service and national foodservice accounts; financial fragility must be checked before promotion beyond Layer 1.
WEST belongs in the broader beverage-program supply chain rather than pure equipment; keep only if later evidence shows chain restaurant, foodservice, extract, or cold-brew capacity leverage.

Need a follow-up pass on commercial refrigeration and beverage-dispensing assets hidden inside large conglomerates or private owners, including Dover Food Retail, Cornelius/Marmon/Berkshire, Welbilt/Ali Group, BUNN, and service contractors.

The strongest version of the node thesis is not simply restaurant equipment demand; it is certified national-chain uptime, installation, maintenance, field service density, and consumables/service attachment.

node: Kitchen equipment, beverage dispensing, refrigeration, service, and labor-saving automation
summary: Expanded the restaurant equipment/service/automation node with a two-lane universe. The reference anchor is Middleby, a direct commercial foodservice equipment supplier to QSR and full-service restaurants. The underfollowed lane emphasizes less obvious exposures: Farmer Brothers as a micro-cap coffee/beverage equipment service network, Westrock Coffee as a beverage-program and extract/cold-brew capacity supplier adjacent to dispensing demand, and Richtech Robotics as a speculative service-robotics automation candidate. The key chokepoint hypothesis remains that national uptime, field service, customer certification, and installed-base support may matter more than equipment manufacturing alone.
